bindings.label: A 5-month-old girl had fever followed by seizure and left-sided body weakness
Patient is a 5-month-old girl, born full-term via vaginal delivery, with no prior history of seizures and age-appropriate motor and language development
Parents reported she was in her usual state of health and behaving normally before developing fever; a few hours after fever onset, she experienced a seizure
She was brought to Gandhi Memorial Hospital (GMH), Rewa, while actively seizing and was administered intravenous midazolam, phenytoin, valproate, and levetiracetam
The seizure lasted approximately 10–15 hours in total; following the seizure she exhibited weakness on the left side of her body

By the third day of hospitalization, her mental status had improved but she still showed left-sided hemiparesis and was not speaking spontaneously; over the next four days her condition began to improve with continued antiepileptic treatment
MRI shows right hemicerebral diffusion restriction
